extracted.intended_audience: receiving Offices, International Searching Authorities, patent applicants (agents/attorneys) filing under the PCT
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural criteria for filing, priority restoration, corrections, searches, fees, and international search report requirements under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT). Applicable to receiving Offices, International Searching Authorities, and applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for restoration of right of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office shall restore the right of priority if it finds that a criterion applied by it ('criterion for restoration') is satisfied, namely, that the failure to file the international application within the priority period: (i) occurred in spite of due care required by the circumstances having been taken; or (ii) was unintentional. Each receiving Office shall apply at least one of those criteria and may apply both of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration is discretionary subject to the chosen criterion(s) by each Office; the Office may apply either or both criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for requesting restoration
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for restoration under Rule 26 bis.3 must be filed within two months from the date on which the priority period expired, provided that where applicant requests early publication or technical preparations for publication are completed, late submissions may be considered not in time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request, notice or fee submitted after technical preparations for international publication have been completed shall be considered as not having been submitted or paid in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of a restoration request
rubrics_metrics.description: A request shall be filed with the receiving Office within the applicable time limit; shall state the reasons for the failure to file within the priority period; and preferably be accompanied by any declaration or other evidence required under paragraph (f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Office may require a declaration or other evidence to support the statement of reasons; applicant should supply reasons and supporting evidence where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of a missing priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a priority claim in respect of the earlier application is not contained in the international application, the applicant shall submit, within the applicable time limit, a notice under Rule 26 bis.1(a) adding the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding the priority claim is a distinct procedural step and must comply with the same time limit applicable to restoration requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for restoration requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office may subject a request for restoration to the payment, for its own benefit, of a fee for requesting restoration, payable within the applicable time limit. The amount, if any, shall be fixed by the receiving Office. The time limit for payment of the fee may be extended by the Office for up to two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should check the receiving Office's rules for whether a restoration fee applies and payment deadlines/extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office decision, notifications and transmission obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office shall promptly: notify the International Bureau of receipt of a restoration request; make a decision upon the request; notify the applicant and the International Bureau of its decision and the criterion for restoration upon which the decision was based; and, subject to limits, transmit to the International Bureau all documents received relating to the request (including request, statement of reasons, declarations or evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires prompt administrative handling and clear notification of the basis for decisions; transmission to IB is standard unless withholding is justified (see withholding criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withholding transmission of documents to the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office shall, upon a reasoned request by the applicant or on its own decision, not transmit documents or parts thereof received in relation to a restoration request if it finds that: (i) the document or part does not obviously serve the purpose of informing the public about the international application; (ii) publication or public access would clearly prejudice the personal or economic interests of any person; and (iii) there is no prevailing public interest to have access. The Office shall notify the IB accordingly when it withholds documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a narrowly drawn privacy/protection exception; Offices must reason and notify the IB when withholding.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau publication of priority information and applicant submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the receiving Office or the International Bureau has made a declaration under paragraph (b) or where the priority claim has not been considered void only because paragraph (c) applies, the IB shall publish, together with the international application, information concerning the priority claim as prescribed by the Administrative Instructions, as well as any information submitted by the applicant concerning such priority claim which is received by the IB prior to completion of technical preparations for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may request IB publication of corrections/additions subject to fee (see Rule 26bis.2(e)); timing relative to technical preparations is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction or addition of declarations (Rule 4.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may correct or add to any declaration referred to in Rule 4.17 by a notice submitted to the International Bureau within 16 months from the priority date; any notice received after that time is considered received on the last day if it reaches IB before technical preparations for publication are completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 16-month limit applies; late-but-before-technical-preparation submissions may be treated as timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of declarations — invitation to correct wording/signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the receiving Office or the International Bureau finds that any declaration referred to in Rule 4.17 is not worded as required or (for declaration of inventorship) not signed as required, the Office or IB may invite the applicant to correct the declaration within a time limit of 16 months from the priority date. Late corrections received by IB are handled under the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Offices and the IB can request formal correction; applicants should respond within the 16-month window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction or addition of indications (Rule 4.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may correct or add to any indication referred to in Rule 4.11 by notice to the IB within 16 months from the priority date; late notices are considered received on the last day if they reach IB before technical preparations for publication are completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same 16-month timing and technical-preparation exception as declarations; late corrections handled by Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of fees for lack of payment (Rule 27.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Article 14(3)(a) 'fees prescribed under Article 3(4)(iv)' means: the transmittal fee (Rule 14), the international filing fee (Rule 15.1), the search fee (Rule 16), and, where required, the late payment fee (Rule 16 bis.2). For Article 14(3)(a) and (b), 'the fee prescribed under Article 4(2)' means the international filing fee (Rule 15.1) and, where required, the late payment fee (Rule 16 bis.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which specific fees count for Article 14 non-payment findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau note on certain defects (Rule 28.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If IB finds that the international application contains any defects referred to in Article 14(1)(a)(i), (ii) or (v), IB shall bring such defects to the attention of the receiving Office. The receiving Office shall, unless it disagrees, proceed as provided in Article 14(1)(b) and Rule 26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB flags defects to the receiving Office; the RO generally follows unless it disagrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and procedures when application is considered withdrawn (Rule 29.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the receiving Office declares that the international application is considered withdrawn (for listed failures), the receiving Office shall transmit the record copy (unless already transmitted) and any correction offered to IB; notify applicant and IB; not transmit the search copy (or notify ISA if already transmitted); IB not required to notify applicant of receipt of record copy; and no international publication shall occur if notification reaches IB before technical preparations for publication completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists concrete administrative actions following a withdrawal declaration; timing relative to technical preparations affects publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of intent to make a declaration under Article 14(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before issuing any declaration under Article 14(4) the receiving Office shall notify the applicant of its intent and reasons; the applicant may, if disagreeing, submit arguments within two months from the date of notification. If the intended declaration concerns an element for which incorporation by reference confirmation under Rule 20.6(a) is needed, the notification shall invite the applicant to confirm accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides applicant an opportunity to respond within a 2-month window; special procedural invitation for incorporation-by-reference elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant prior art for the international search
rubrics_metrics.description: For Article 15(2), relevant prior art consists of everything made available to the public anywhere in the world by written disclosure (including drawings/illustrations) capable of assisting in determining novelty and inventive step, provided the making available occurred prior to the international filing date. Written disclosures that refer to oral disclosures, use, exhibition etc shall be separately mentioned in the international search report when the making available occurred prior to the filing date. Published applications/patents whose publication date is same as or later than but whose filing date (or claimed priority date) is earlier than the international filing date and which would have been relevant if published prior to the filing date shall be specially mentioned in the search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search reports must note prior art timing nuances; both publication and filing/priority dates matter for relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields to be covered by the international search
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search shall cover all technical fields and be carried out on the basis of all search files which may contain material pertinent to the invention. Not only shall the art in which the invention is classifiable be searched but also analogous arts regardless of classification. Whether arts are analogous should be considered in light of the necessary essential function or use of the invention. The international search shall also embrace subject matter generally recognized as equivalent to the subject matter of the claimed invention for all or certain features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search scope is broad: include analogous arts determined by essential function/use and equivalents to claimed subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation of the international search
rubrics_metrics.description: International search shall be made on the basis of the claims, with due regard to the description and drawings and with particular emphasis on the inventive concept towards which the claims are directed. As far as possible and reasonable, the search shall cover the entire subject matter to which the claims are directed or to which they might reasonably be expected to be directed after amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims are primary but description/drawings and conceivable amended claim scope must be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of minimum documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'minimum documentation' referred to in Article 15(4) consists of: (i) the 'national patent documents' as specified; (ii) published international (PCT) applications, published regional applications and patents and inventors' certificates; (iii) such other published items of non-patent literature as ISAs shall agree upon and which shall be published in a list by the IB when agreed upon or changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum documentation is a defined set including national patent collections, PCT/regional publications and agreed non-patent literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/list of 'national patent documents'
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to paragraphs, 'national patent documents' shall include: (i) patents issued in and after 1920 by France, former Reichspatentamt of Germany, Japan, former Soviet Union, Switzerland (French/German only), UK, USA; (ii) patents issued by FRG, PRC, Republic of Korea, Russian Federation; (iii) patent applications published in/after 1920 in those countries; (iv) inventors' certificates issued by former Soviet Union; (v) utility certificates issued by France and published applications for utility certificates; (vi) such patents/applications in any other country after 1920 as are in English/French/German/Spanish and in which no priority is claimed, provided the national Office places these at disposal of each ISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which national patent collections must be included in minimum documentation; language and date criteria apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum requirements for International Searching Authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum requirements (Article 16(3)(c)) are: (i) the national Office or intergovernmental organization must have at least 100 full-time employees with sufficient technical qualifications to carry out searches; (ii) must have in its possession, or access to, at least the minimum documentation (Rule 34) properly arranged for search purposes; (iii) must have staff capable of searching required technical fields and language facilities to understand at least languages of the minimum documentation; (iv) must have a quality management system and internal review arrangements in accordance with the common rules of international search; (v) must hold an appointment as an International Preliminary Examining Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISAs must meet staffing, documentation, language, quality management and appointment criteria to be competent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling missing or defective title
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application does not contain a title and the receiving Office has notified ISA that it invited applicant to correct, the ISA shall proceed with the international search unless and until it receives notification that the application is considered withdrawn. If ISA has not received such notification and finds no title or non-complying title, it shall itself establish a title in the language of publication or, if a translation was transmitted and ISA so wishes, in the language of that translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISAs normally proceed despite missing title; they may establish a title for publication language if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling missing, defective or modified abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: If no abstract is contained and the receiving Office has invited the applicant to correct, the ISA shall proceed with search unless application is withdrawn. If ISA has not received notification and the abstract is missing or non-complying, the ISA shall establish an abstract in the language of publication or, if a translation was transmitted and ISA so wishes, in the language of that translation. The applicant may, until one month from date of mailing of the international search report, submit proposed modifications or comments and the Authority shall decide whether to modify the abstract accordingly; where Authority modifies, it shall notify IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants have one month after mailing of search report to propose abstract modifications; ISA can establish/modify abstracts as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter not required to be searched (Article 17(2)(a)(i) exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: No ISA shall be required to search if, and to the extent which, subject matter is: (i) scientific and mathematical theories; (ii) plant/animal varieties or essentially biological processes for their production (other than microbiological processes and products of such processes); (iii) schemes, rules or methods of doing business, performing purely mental acts or playing games; (iv) methods for treatment of human/animal body by surgery or therapy and diagnostic methods; (v) mere presentations of information; (vi) computer programs to the extent the ISA is not equipped to search prior art concerning such programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates exclusions where ISA may decline to search; applicability depends on equipment/competence for some categories (e.g., computer programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to pay additional fees for lack of unity (content and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invitation to pay additional fees under Article 17(3)(a) shall: (i) specify reasons why the application is not considered to comply with unity of invention; (ii) invite the applicant to pay additional fees within one month from the date of invitation and indicate the amount; (iii) invite the applicant to pay, where applicable, the protest fee within one month and indicate the amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invitation must explain lack-of-unity reasons and set one-month payment deadlines for fees and protest fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional fees and protest procedure for lack of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of additional fees due for searching shall be determined by the competent ISA; additional fees payable directly to the ISA. Any applicant may pay under protest accompanied by a reasoned statement that the application complies with unity or that fee amount is excessive. The protest shall be examined by a review body within the ISA which, if it finds protest justified, shall order total or partial reimbursement of additional fees. On request, the texts of both protest and decision may be notified to designated Offices with the international search report; applicant shall submit any translation thereof with the furnishing of the translation required under Article 22. The membership of the review body may include, but not be limited to, the person who made the decision under protest. Examination of protest may be subjected to a protest fee, refundable if protest entirely justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a mechanism for contesting additional fees; review body procedures and possible protest fee apply; reimbursement if justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional fees for missing parts or late-corrected elements
rubrics_metrics.description: ISA may invite the applicant to pay additional fees where a missing part or correct element/part is included in or considered to have been contained in the international application only after it has begun to draw up the international search report. The invitation shall invite payment within one month and indicate the amount. Amount determined by ISA but not exceed the search fee; fees payable directly to ISA. If paid within the prescribed time limit, ISA shall establish the international search report including the missing part or corrected element or part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional fees compensate for late inclusion of material after search has started; cap equals the search fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking into account results of an earlier search
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant has requested ISA to take into account results of an earlier search and has complied with Rule 12 bis.1: (i) if earlier search was by same ISA or same Office acting as ISA, the ISA shall, to the extent possible, take those results into account; (ii) if earlier search was by another ISA or Office, the ISA may take those results into account. More generally, where applicant claims priority of earlier applications with earlier search by same ISA/Office, ISA shall, to the extent possible, take those earlier results into account. Where receiving Office has transmitted results of earlier search or classification or such copy is available (e.g., digital library), ISA may take those into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISAs should use earlier searches where available and appropriate, especially when done by the same authority; transmissions from ROs facilitate this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for establishing the international search report
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit for establishing the international search report or the declaration referred to in Article 17(2)(a) shall be three months from the receipt of the search copy by the ISA, or nine months from the priority date, whichever expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two alternative cutoffs: 3 months from search copy receipt or 9 months from priority date; whichever is later governs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and language requirements of the international search report
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search report shall be dated and indicate the date on which the international search was actually completed and the filing date of any earlier application whose priority is claimed (or earliest among them). It shall contain classification at least according to the International Patent Classification, effected by the ISA. Every international search report and any declaration under Article 17(2)(a) shall be in the language in which the international application is to be published, provided that if a translation of the application into another language was transmitted and the ISA so wishes, the report and declaration may be in the language of that translation; further language exception rules apply where translations furnished under Rule 12.4 are not accepted by the ISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must state completion date, priority filing dates, IPC classification, and be in the publication language (with specified translation exceptions). Also must identify the ISA, application number, applicant name and filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and citation content of the international search report
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search report shall identify the ISA which established it by indicating its name, and the international application number, the name of the applicant, and the international filing date. The report shall also contain citations (as required elsewhere in the Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard metadata and citations must be present for proper identification and prior art references.
